title: Plea relief: waiver door first
signal: The stem gives a guilty plea and a later motion to set it aside.
student_move: Ask which answer attacks the knowing and voluntary waiver.
tiny_rule: Missing jury-trial understanding attacks the plea; earlier motions, factual guilt, and prosecutor files are neighboring doors.
trap: Choosing the unresolved pretrial motion because it appears first and has a concrete delay fact.

title: Grand jury remedy gate
signal: Grand jury + counsel access or illegally seized evidence + motion to dismiss indictment.
student_move: Ask: is this a dismissal rule, or just a violation/suppression fact?
tiny_rule: Grand jury indictment survives both no-inside-counsel and illegally seized evidence defects.
trap: Treating constitutional violation language as automatic dismissal.

title: Split before you suppress
signal: Two evidence batches with a government-contact event in the middle.
student_move: Mark first search / agent event / second search. Reject all-or-none answers unless the same legal layer governs both.
tiny_rule: Private first; government-induced second.
trap: Treating stipulated illegality as automatic suppression.

title: Element or Defense?
signal: A jury instruction puts the burden on the defendant for two different issues.
student_move: Underline the statute words. If the issue is inside the offense definition, state burden. If it is a separate defensive excuse, defendant burden may be allowed.
tiny_rule: Elements stay with the prosecution; true affirmative defenses may be assigned to the defendant.
trap: Picking 'both' whenever the defendant gets any burden.

title: Do not treat preliminary hearings as jeopardy
signal: preliminary hearing + dismissal + later indictment
student_move: Ask whether trial began before applying double-jeopardy bars.
tiny_rule: No trial start, no jeopardy attachment.
trap: Correct result with wrong conviction/acquittal trigger.

title: Later Death vs Acquitted Predicate
signal: Victim dies after first trial; later felony-murder charge follows.
student_move: Ask what felony the murder theory must prove.
tiny_rule: Later death is not a free pass to relitigate an acquitted predicate.
trap: Choosing the later-death/no-murder-jeopardy answer without checking the predicate.

title: Privilege is not just another trial evidence rule
signal: Lawyer hires nonlawyer helper + grand jury subpoena.
student_move: Ask whether the helper is inside the lawyer's legal-representation team before applying ordinary grand-jury evidence-rule shortcuts.
tiny_rule: Lawyer's representative can be privileged; grand jury does not erase privilege.
trap: The consultant is not an attorney / grand jury evidence rules are relaxed.

title: Suppressing the statement: stay on the statement layer
signal: The call names an admission/confession, but answer choices talk about search, pursuit, or emergency.
student_move: Ask which choice explains why the statement itself can or cannot be used.
tiny_rule: Statement call first. Search/arrest facts are traps unless they connect to the statement rule.
trap: Choosing the dramatic police-entry fact over the statement-waiver fact.

title: Custody is not enough; find the police-created elicitation.
signal: Statement made after Miranda + request for lawyer + police arrange someone else to talk.
student_move: Do not stop at custody, lawyer request, or privacy. Ask what police did to cause the statement.
tiny_rule: Post-invocation police-arranged elicitation is the suppression hook.
trap: The student picks B because it says lawyer, or C because it says private conversation.

title: Fake object, real criminal purpose
signal: The object is fake, but the actor believed it was contraband.
student_move: Split actors, then apply the attempt-impossibility Gold Key.
tiny_rule: Belief plus substantial step can create attempt even when completion was factually impossible.
trap: No real contraband means no attempt.

title: Two defendants, two liability links
signal: Direct seller plus owner are both convicted.
student_move: Ask what each conviction needs.
tiny_rule: Strict = no mens rea needed. Vicarious = owner liable for employee act.
trap: Stopping after the first theory that explains only one defendant.

title: Retreat trap: force type first
signal: Stem says retreat jurisdiction; answers split on retreat.
student_move: Identify whether the defendant used deadly or nondeadly force.
tiny_rule: Nondeadly force does not require retreat.
trap: Treating retreat doctrine as automatic.

title: Mistake Changes Which Gate?
signal: Multiple answer choices all contain a plausible mistake.
student_move: Sort the mistake by what it changes.
tiny_rule: Mistake wins only if it negates a required mental state or recognized justification gate.
trap: Picking the most sympathetic or careful defendant.

title: Source beats effect on intoxication instructions
signal: The stem already says the drug influenced the defendant.
student_move: Do not ask which fact proves stronger drug effect. Ask which fact makes the intoxication involuntary.
tiny_rule: General intent plus intoxication: voluntary loses; involuntary can matter.
trap: D feels best because it says uncontrollable rages.

title: Defense before severity
signal: A serious injury appears, but the stem also shows the defendant was under attack.
student_move: Before selecting the biggest crime label, ask whether a defense or missing intent knocks it out.
tiny_rule: Most serious means most serious surviving offense, not worst harm.
trap: serious injury overpowers self-defense and intent checks

title: Mental-state target check
signal: Answer borrows intent from one crime to prove another crime.
student_move: Circle the noun after the intent word and the noun after the charged offense. If they differ, slow down.
tiny_rule: Mens rea must be aimed at the charged result or element.
trap: Intent to steal Mary’s car gets used to prove malicious damage to Lydia’s store.

title: Control beats personal-act framing in public-welfare officer questions.
signal: CEO/general manager delegated operations; strict-liability regulatory statute.
student_move: Ask who had responsibility/control, not only who physically did the prohibited act.
tiny_rule: Responsible-control position can carry liability for strict regulatory offenses.
trap: The personal criminal-liability slogan is powerful but incomplete in the public-welfare officer frame.

title: Reasonable belief beats secret intent
signal: Attacker secretly meant less harm than the defendant reasonably perceived.
student_move: Lock onto what the defendant reasonably believed at the moment force was used.
tiny_rule: Self-defense uses defendant's reasonable belief, not the attacker's hidden plan.
trap: Choosing C because Paul did not actually intend harm.

title: Advice is not the defense; belief may defeat the element.
signal: Statute says knowing / belief / purpose, and facts include advice from a lawyer or official-looking order.
student_move: Ask whether the advice is offered as a freestanding defense or as evidence negating the mental state.
tiny_rule: Mens rea answer beats advice-of-counsel answer when the statute itself requires knowledge.
trap: Convicting because private attorney advice is not a defense.

title: Attempt changes the completed-offense shortcut
signal: The target offense is strict liability, but the charge is attempt.
student_move: Circle attempt. Then ask what intent the attempt answer requires.
tiny_rule: Under the supplied exam rule, no underage intent defeats attempted statutory rape.
trap: Using completed-offense strict liability to answer attempt.

title: Open Door Is Retreat Bait
signal: Defender is in his own home, but the stem shows an escape path.
student_move: Do not punish the defender for failing to flee until the retreat rule is confirmed.
tiny_rule: Home + imminent deadly threat = no duty to retreat.
trap: Picking conviction because the defender could have left.

title: Mistake Target: Fact vs Regulation
signal: Knowingly + regulatory offense + answer choices about age, ID, and legal knowledge.
student_move: Ask what the defendant was mistaken about: the buyer's age/status, or the rule itself.
tiny_rule: Age/status mistake helps; unused ID and legal-knowledge mistakes do not.
trap: Students pick fake ID because it sounds like a real-world excuse.

title: Do not let voluntary adjacent acts replace the charged voluntary act.
signal: Police physically create one statutory element.
student_move: Name the charged conduct element and ask whether that element was voluntary.
tiny_rule: Voluntary intoxication or voluntary loudness does not supply voluntary public appearance.
trap: Picking D because the defendant did choose to be loud.

title: Definition-first attempt impossibility
signal: Attempt call + supplied statutory definition + intended completed act fails an element even if completed.
student_move: Test the intended completed facts against the crime definition before choosing an impossibility answer.
tiny_rule: If the completed intended act would not be a crime, call legal impossibility.
trap: Picking factual impossibility because the physical plan failed.

title: Voluntary intoxication scope quartet
signal: Same intoxication evidence; two charges; choices divide by count.
student_move: Tag the charges: specific-intent count gets the evidence; general-intent count does not.
tiny_rule: Specific intent only.
trap: The visible injury count feels like the place intoxication matters, but the attempted murder intent is the real target.

title: Knew wrong, could not conform
signal: The stem gives both right-wrong knowledge and irresistible compulsion.
student_move: Do not pick M'Naghten just because the issue is insanity. Match the compulsion fact to ALI/MPC.
tiny_rule: M'Naghten = cognitive. ALI/MPC = cognitive or volitional.
trap: Famous-test bias.

title: Force gets robbery started; intent still has to be there.
signal: Robbery charge with force plus defendant thinks the property is his.
student_move: Separate the force element from the theft-intent element.
tiny_rule: Force/fear does not substitute for intent to steal.
trap: Convicting just because force was used or because intoxication was voluntary.

title: Two-motion homicide call
signal: The defendant moves for acquittal or, alternatively, a manslaughter instruction.
student_move: Split the ruling: causation for acquittal; provocation for instruction.
tiny_rule: Murder sufficiency does not automatically deny a lesser-included instruction.
trap: D

title: Most serious degree: do not stop at true lower homicide
signal: Degree-ladder answer set with attractive felony-murder choice
student_move: Rank all surviving homicide degrees before selecting
tiny_rule: True lower degree loses to higher surviving degree
trap: Stopping at felony murder because the death happened during a felony

title: Chain-Setter Murder
signal: Defendant manipulates another person into a foreseeable deadly confrontation.
student_move: Do not ask only who fired. Ask who created the deadly chain and whether the death was foreseeable.
tiny_rule: Extreme reckless causation can beat shooter/accomplice traps.
trap: Picking transferred intent or not-guilty because the defendant did not shoot.

title: Planned provocation blocks the downgrade
signal: Defendant goes to the scene hoping the victim will attack first.
student_move: Treat later self-defense and manslaughter answers as traps unless the stem shows withdrawal or a truly new escalation.
tiny_rule: Do not let the bait fact erase the setup fact.
trap: Paul had a knife, so self-defense feels intuitive.

title: No intent to kill does not automatically mean manslaughter
signal: Defendant denies intent to kill, but deliberately creates a lethal risk.
student_move: Do not stop at the denial of intent. Ask whether the top homicide rung is unlocked by extreme recklessness.
tiny_rule: Extreme life-endangering recklessness can be murder.
trap: Choosing involuntary manslaughter because the killing was unintended.

title: Fire-death offense bundle
signal: A deliberate gasoline-fire fact pattern plus two charged offenses.
student_move: Check arson column and homicide column separately.
tiny_rule: Dwelling fire + death can be both arson and murder.
trap: Picking manslaughter because there was no stated intent to kill.

title: Reckless homicide: defense axis check
signal: Manslaughter + intoxication + mistaken self-defense
student_move: Cut intoxication-as-no-risk; then clash actual danger against reasonable apprehension.
tiny_rule: Recklessness survives voluntary intoxication; self-defense turns on reasonable apprehension, not actual danger alone.
trap: Picking C because it states the true fact that there was no actual danger.

title: First-Degree Murder Requires Murder First
signal: See a question asking about first-degree murder — always check whether murder exists before analyzing degree.
student_move: Before evaluating poison or premeditation, ask: does the defendant have malice aforethought? If not, the answer is 'no murder' regardless of the aggravators.
tiny_rule: No malice = no murder = no first-degree murder
trap: Jumping to the degree analysis without confirming the underlying crime

title: No intent does not end murder
signal: A killing is accidental in aim, but the defendant knowingly creates a lethal risk to people.
student_move: Do not drop automatically to manslaughter. Ask whether the facts show extreme disregard for human life.
tiny_rule: Known extreme risk can supply murder-level malice.
trap: Accident equals involuntary manslaughter.

title: Do not let instant erase cool.
signal: First-degree answer quotes 'any length of time' but skips 'cool reflection.'
student_move: Circle the mental-state adjective, not just the timing phrase.
tiny_rule: Brief deliberation still must be cool deliberation.
trap: B

title: Do not let the dead victim erase the attempt victim.
signal: One target survives; another person dies.
student_move: Make two boxes: target branch and death branch.
tiny_rule: Attempt does not need completion; homicide does need death.
trap: Picking the completed-death answer and dropping attempt.

title: Implied Malice + Accomplice Homicide
signal: Loaded gun fired into a crowded place during an armed robbery, with felony murder abolished.
student_move: Do not let the felony-murder abolition erase implied-malice murder or accomplice liability.
tiny_rule: Depraved indifference can supply malice, and an armed partner can be liable for a foreseeable homicide.
trap: The dominant trap concedes the shooter's murder but wrongly cuts off the partner.

title: Fatal shot first; range answer second
signal: The stem separates earlier defensive force from the fatal act.
student_move: Circle the fatal act, then ask whether the stem settled the murder/manslaughter axis.
tiny_rule: No fear at the fatal shot cuts self-defense; unresolved heat of passion leaves murder or manslaughter.
trap: Picking manslaughter only because provocation is vivid.

title: Protected victim is not the conspiracy partner
signal: The only alleged coconspirator is the person the statute protects.
student_move: Do not stop at agreement. Ask whether that person can be the guilty partner for this offense.
tiny_rule: Protected victim defeats conspiracy with that victim as the only partner.
trap: Wharton's Rule and generic minor incapacity feel more familiar but answer the wrong route.

title: Attempt by using another person
signal: Defendant wants crime done but routes it through another person.
student_move: Ask for the defendant's intent and the defendant's step. Then ask whether the wrong answer is demanding completion.
tiny_rule: Attempt = intent + substantial step; no completed harm required.
trap: Recklessness, no imminent danger, or principal's lesser crime.

title: Guilty mind, innocent hand
signal: A child or mistaken person physically performs the taking.
student_move: Do not stop at the immediate actor’s innocence. Route the guilty mind through the innocent hand.
tiny_rule: Innocent actor does not block liability for the person who caused the act with the required mens rea.
trap: Attempt-only or accessory-only labels.

title: After-the-fact means after the crime
signal: A helper moves, hides, lies, shelters the offender, or removes a witness after a completed crime.
student_move: Do not ask whether the principal was convicted. Ask whether the helper acted to hinder apprehension, trial, conviction, or punishment.
tiny_rule: Post-crime aid + knowledge + purpose to hinder = accessory after the fact.
trap: Mistaking indictment or conviction status for an element.

title: Do not let robbery swallow miles of movement
signal: Substantial forced travel before the taking.
student_move: Ask whether the movement is the felony's mere handhold or a separate substantial removal.
tiny_rule: MPC kidnapping can rest on substantial forced removal to facilitate a felony or flight.
trap: A

title: Suppression chain: event, evidence, reason
signal: A choice gives the right result but a reason that does not connect to the evidence.
student_move: Ask what evidence is being suppressed and which fact made that evidence lawfully obtained.
tiny_rule: In Fourth Amendment questions, match the justification to the challenged evidence, not merely to the officer's general authority.
trap: Arrest warrant = all evidence admissible.

title: Bank records: interest first, process second
signal: Agents obtain account records from a bank.
student_move: Ask whether the defendant has a Fourth Amendment interest before arguing warrant, subpoena, or suppression.
tiny_rule: Miller bank records are bank business records; no Fourth Amendment suppression right belongs to the depositor.
trap: Treating personal finance privacy as Fourth Amendment privacy.

title: Voluntary intoxication: specific-intent only
signal: The stem says the offense requires intentional contact but no further purpose.
student_move: Classify the offense before applying intoxication.
tiny_rule: Voluntary intoxication does not excuse general intent.
trap: Treating drunkenness, blackout, or no memory as a universal intent defense.

title: Property-crime taxonomy: title, possession, custody
signal: Choices name larceny by trick, embezzlement, and false pretenses.
student_move: Find what the victim transferred.
tiny_rule: Title/ownership by deceit = false pretenses; possession-only by deceit = larceny by trick; lawful custody then conversion = embezzlement.
trap: Students stop at the visible lie instead of classifying the transfer.

title: Defense of others: reasonable appearance beats hidden truth
signal: Intervener reasonably but mistakenly protects the apparent victim.
student_move: Do not ask who was actually entitled to self-defense until you know the rule frame.
tiny_rule: Majority rule = reasonable belief; alter ego = actual rights.
trap: Hidden-truth answer feels precise but answers the wrong rule frame.

title: Wharton Count Check
signal: Wharton's Rule plus extra people in the agreement
student_move: Count required participants first; count actual agreement participants second.
tiny_rule: Extra participants defeat Wharton's Rule.
trap: Stopping at the two-party offense and missing the extra-party exception.

title: Miranda Fruit Is Not Fourth-Amendment Fruit
signal: Unwarned but voluntary statement leads police to a physical object.
student_move: Pin the offered evidence: statement or object.
tiny_rule: Statement out; voluntary-statement physical fruit generally in.
trap: Importing all-fruits suppression from Fourth Amendment doctrine.

title: Warnings are not a pressure shield
signal: Stem gives Miranda warnings and then coercive pressure facts.
student_move: Separate warning/form facts from voluntariness facts.
tiny_rule: Coercion can defeat admissibility even after warnings.
trap: Picking the warning answer because it sounds procedurally clean.

title: Bad arrest is not automatic dismissal
signal: Unlawful arrest + motion to dismiss + independent evidence
student_move: Separate the violation from the requested remedy.
tiny_rule: Suppress tainted evidence when applicable; do not dismiss charges supported by independent evidence.
trap: Treating illegality as automatic case erasure.

title: Plain feel: immediate apparentness, not tactile investigation
signal: Lawful frisk; nonweapon object; officer keeps feeling it to identify it.
student_move: Stop the frisk at the moment the officer knows the item is not a weapon unless contraband is already immediately apparent.
tiny_rule: Manipulation to identify contraband breaks plain feel.
trap: Treating Terry frisk as permission to search for drugs.

title: Duress requires now-pressure.
signal: Future threat, remote threatener, time to seek help.
student_move: Cut fear-only and family-only answers; keep the answer that checks imminence.
tiny_rule: Duress is immediate-threat plus no reasonable escape, not fear alone.
trap: Sympathy for a believable family threat.

title: Same offense, new label
signal: Police say they only want to ask about a smaller version of the charged incident.
student_move: Do not stop at the label. Compare the factual event and offense substance.
tiny_rule: Post-charge Sixth Amendment protection follows the same offense in substance.
trap: The label-only answer sounds precise but is too shallow.

title: Fact mistake / law mistake split
signal: One actor misunderstands ownership facts; another understands facts but misunderstands legality.
student_move: First label each mistake as fact or law, then apply the specific-intent Gold Key.
tiny_rule: Specific-intent fact mistake can negate intent; law mistake generally cannot.
trap: Treating all sincere mistakes the same or requiring reasonableness for every mistake.

title: Insanity tests: cognition vs volition
signal: Stem gives M'Naghten plus irresistible impulse.
student_move: Match facts to lanes before picking.
tiny_rule: Know-wrong = cognition; cannot-conform = volition.
trap: Treating one lane as the whole insanity defense.

title: Misdemeanor label is not a death cause
signal: A misdemeanor is followed by a death from a separate event.
student_move: Ask whether the misdemeanor produced the death, not merely whether it came first.
tiny_rule: No cause link, no misdemeanor manslaughter.
trap: Counting chronology as causation.

title: Person warrant vs place warrant
signal: Arrest warrant for suspect + suspect inside someone else's home.
student_move: Ask whose home the police entered.
tiny_rule: Third-party home requires a search warrant for that home or a valid exception.
trap: Arrest warrant portability.

title: Actor Before Privacy
signal: A private person searches, finds evidence, and later calls police.
student_move: Ask whether the search was done by the government or its agent before analyzing privacy in the place searched.
tiny_rule: Purely private searches do not trigger Fourth Amendment exclusion.
trap: Closed-container privacy feels dispositive, but the actor threshold comes first.
